corpus.evidence: fixtures in the rule's own suite plus an adversarial wave.

oracle.evidence: no independent decider. CodeQL js/client-side-unvalidated-url-redirection is the comparable analysis.

effectiveFp.evidence: not measured under the formal protocol.

reachability.evidence: the rule requires a STEERABLE url value at the sink, which is the right shape, but it does not resolve a path from a named untrusted source the way no-timing-unsafe-compare does.

adversarial.evidence: a 6-case wave scored 5/6. The self-reload exemption held: a genuine `window.location.assign(window.location.href)` is silent, and a cross-frame `top.location.href` still reports. The miss is the `w.location` sink — see knownGaps.

realSource.evidence: measured on 8 pinned repositories; the self-reload exemption was driven by okta-signin-widget transformTerminalTransaction.ts, whose own comment reads 'Load the current page URI again to get a new state token'.

partition.evidence: url-navigation-partition.matrix.test.ts lints one snippet with all four URL rules enabled and asserts the exact set that reports. This is 1 of 3 records in the repo with partition met.

knownGaps.summary: a Location reached through an unproven local — `w.location.assign(req.query.next)` — is silent, including for plainly tainted input.
knownGaps.why: the rule resolves the holder rather than matching the spelling, deliberately: `w` cannot be proven a Window without types, and matching any `.location` by name is the name-inference defect this ecosystem gates against. The rule's own partition table nonetheless claims 'any write to a Location or its .href, any spelling of the holder', so the DOC currently overstates the contract.
knownGaps.reopenWhen: either the rule becomes type-aware, or the partition table is corrected to say which holders are resolvable — whichever comes first, and the doc fix is due regardless.

knownGaps.summary: the self-reload exemption compares the printed text of the two Location expressions.
knownGaps.why: both come from the same file, so printed form is exactly the 'same Location object' question at this analysis depth; an alias (`const l = window.location; l.assign(window.location.href)`) would defeat it.
knownGaps.reopenWhen: points-to analysis is available, or an alias case is found on real source.

notes: Seal record OPENED 2026-08-21. `partition` MET here, one of very few — the four-rule URL matrix test predates this work. The adversarial wave surfaced a documentation defect rather than a code one: the partition table promises more than the rule delivers.
